categories.label: Harness engineering lessons from frontier labs and experts

entries.name: Anthropic: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
entries.what_it_is: Engineering post on harness architecture for agents that work across many sessions: initializer agent vs coding agent prompts, JSON feature list with pass/fail status, init.sh environment script, progress file, prescribed session-start sequence (verify dir, read git log and progress, baseline test, pick ONE feature), commit discipline, browser-automation verification.
entries.why_high_leverage: Directly upgrades DAD's agent-instruction and preflight harnesses; the failure modes it names (premature completion, undocumented half-work, state-rediscovery waste) match DAD postflight/lesson observations.
entries.candidate_dad_target: agent_instruction harness family; context-pack session-start guidance; candidate non-negotiable: one-feature-per-session with clean mergeable close.
entries.adoption_gate: Content lessons only, no code import; safe to adapt after human read-through.

entries.name: Martin Fowler: Harness engineering for coding agent users
entries.what_it_is: Framework: harness = everything except the model; feedforward guides vs feedback sensors (governor model, both required); computational (fast, deterministic, pre-commit) vs inferential (LLM judges, post-integration) checks; timing distribution across change lifecycle incl. continuous drift monitoring; 'harnessability' as an environment property (strong typing, module boundaries); variety reduction via service topologies; approved-fixtures pattern; mutation testing to grade sensor quality; what a harness cannot externalize (org memory, aesthetic judgment, load-bearing conventions).
entries.why_high_leverage: The feedforward/feedback and computational/inferential taxonomy is a ready-made upgrade for DAD's coding-harness registry schema; 'harnessability' aligns with DAD's AI-legibility goals; mutation-testing-as-sensor-grading is a concrete new harness family.
entries.candidate_dad_target: coding-harness registry taxonomy fields (guide_or_sensor, computational_or_inferential, lifecycle_stage); new test_quality harness family; ai-legibility lint rationale.
entries.adoption_gate: Conceptual framework; no license issues; adapt vocabulary after human review.

entries.name: OpenAI: Harness engineering with Codex (+ App Server post)
entries.what_it_is: OpenAI's own posts on leveraging Codex in an agent-first world and how the Codex harness/App Server is built. Fetch was 403-blocked this pass; read manually.
entries.why_high_leverage: Second frontier-lab primary source on harness design; comparing Anthropic vs OpenAI harness lessons separates universal patterns from vendor habits.
entries.candidate_dad_target: harness-discovery research packet; cross-check against Anthropic lessons before promoting either.
entries.adoption_gate: Read manually (fetch blocked); lessons only.

entries.name: Finding: the harness is half the score
entries.org: industry analysis of Anthropic system card
entries.what_it_is: Same model scored 57.5% vs 64.7% on Terminal-Bench depending only on which harness ran it (independent Terminus-2 vs vendor CLI) - a 7-point harness-only gap.
entries.why_high_leverage: Quantifies DAD's core bet: harness quality is worth roughly a model-generation upgrade. Useful as the one-line justification for DAD's existence in front-door docs.
entries.candidate_dad_target: docs/CODING_HARNESS_LIBRARY.md rationale; harness evaluation methodology (control for harness when comparing models).
entries.adoption_gate: Verify against the primary system card before quoting numbers downstream.

entries.name: SWE-bench family (Verified / Pro / Multilingual / Live)

categories.label: Test-quality harness techniques (the biggest gap in DAD's current families)

entries.name: Mutation testing as sensor-grading (cargo-mutants; ToB mewt/muton)
entries.what_it_is: Inject bugs, check whether tests catch them. cargo-mutants for Rust; Trail of Bits skills configure mutation campaigns and generate test vectors from surviving mutants. Fowler frames mutation testing as the way to grade feedback-sensor quality; 2026 consensus is it becomes a default for AI-generated code because AI code volume outruns human review.
entries.why_high_leverage: DAD's harness registry has test_performance and test_parity but nothing measuring whether tests would actually catch bugs - the exact false-green risk DAD's red-team lane keeps flagging. Highest-value NEW harness family identified this pass.
entries.candidate_dad_target: NEW harness family test_quality: mutation score on changed surfaces, property-test coverage of contracts, approved-fixtures pattern.
entries.adoption_gate: Tool-by-tool license review; start with cargo-mutants (Rust) and evaluate Python mutation tools separately before recommending one.

entries.name: Property-based testing for AI-written code (proptest / Hypothesis)
entries.what_it_is: Generate inputs against stated invariants instead of example cases; catches the bug classes AI-generated example tests miss (agents write tests that mirror their own implementation assumptions).
entries.why_high_leverage: Property tests are contracts-as-tests - AI-legible and drift-resistant; pairs with DAD's scoring/parity code where invariants are crisp (determinism, idempotence, threshold monotonicity).
entries.candidate_dad_target: test_quality harness family; DAD's own suite already has early property-style tests (scoring monotonicity) to build on.
entries.adoption_gate: Hypothesis (MPL-2.0) and proptest (MIT/Apache) are standard; low risk.

entries.name: PyO3 v0.28 + maturin 1.8 (current state)
entries.what_it_is: Rust bindings for Python + wheel build/publish tooling. Current floor: Rust 1.83+, Python 3.9+. Key 2026 development: py.allow_threads() plus free-threaded Python 3.14 support means Rust extensions can now use all cores without multiprocessing serialization.
entries.why_high_leverage: Free-threaded Python changes the Rust payoff math: parallel Rust hot paths no longer need process pools. Confirms and extends DAD's rust-buildout-guide stage 5.
entries.candidate_dad_target: rust-buildout-guide upgrade (known_upgrades entry): free-threading note, version floors, release-build benchmarking warning.
entries.adoption_gate: Update guide text after verifying version numbers on pyo3.rs; heuristic until checked.

entries.name: Lesson: batch at the call boundary
entries.what_it_is: Most common PyO3 performance failure: calling Rust functions inside a tight Python loop - boundary overhead dominates. Pass all data in one call, iterate in Rust. Also: benchmark release builds only (debug is 10-20x slower); profile first with py-spy/cProfile; move the 5% of code causing 95% of slowdown.
entries.why_high_leverage: The profile-first, 5%-of-code framing exactly matches the guide's staged path; the call-boundary rule is the missing gotcha in stage 5.
entries.candidate_dad_target: rust-buildout-guide stage 5 gotchas; candidate py-idiom pairing with cprofile card.
entries.adoption_gate: None beyond human read-through.

entries.name: Exemplars: Ruff, uv, Polars, Pydantic v2 core, HF tokenizers, orjson
entries.what_it_is: Production Python-facing libraries with Rust cores via PyO3 - the proven shape of Python-to-Rust: Python API surface, Rust engine.
entries.why_high_leverage: Each is a readable case study of the exact migration DAD's guide stages; Astral's ruff/uv also demonstrate Rust CLI distribution killing Python environment drift - relevant to shipping asset-dir itself as a binary someday.
entries.candidate_dad_target: rust-buildout-guide exemplar section (already lists them; add repo links as source_refs).
entries.adoption_gate: Study only.

entries.why_high_leverage: The canonical structured path for agents AND humans leveling up; the Idiomatic Rust module maps directly onto the guide's rs-idiom cards.
entries.candidate_dad_target: rust-buildout-guide learning-resources section (new); agent context-pack pointer for Rust tasks.
entries.adoption_gate: Apache-2.0 course; link freely, do not copy content into DAD.

entries.name: Cargo quality stack: nextest, semver-checks, miri, proptest, criterion, insta, cargo-mutants
entries.what_it_is: The 2026 Rust quality toolchain: cargo-nextest (faster test runner), cargo-semver-checks (API-break linting, being merged into cargo itself, 10x perf improvements landed), miri (UB detection), proptest (property tests), criterion (benchmarks), insta (snapshot tests), cargo-mutants (mutation).
entries.why_high_leverage: This is the concrete answer to 'develop Rust out as a language': a repo with this stack wired is maximally harnessable in Fowler's sense - every check is a computational sensor an agent can run. semver-checks merging into cargo signals which tools are becoming platform.
entries.candidate_dad_target: rust-buildout-guide repo_conventions ci section upgrade; future rust repo template; test_quality harness family (Rust lane).
entries.adoption_gate: Standard OSS licenses; verify each before templating into downstream repos.
